extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors preparing and submitting manuscripts to Herpetological Conservation and Biology (herpetology/conservation biology)
extracted.subtask_description: Detailed author instructions for preparing, formatting, and submitting manuscripts to the journal Herpetological Conservation and Biology, including scope, acceptable topics, style, review process, and file requirements. Targets researchers (amphibian/reptile ecology, natural history, conservation) preparing manuscripts for this specific journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of journal
rubrics_metrics.description: Herpetological Conservation and Biology is an open-access, peer-reviewed, international journal that publishes original research, reviews, perspectives, and correspondence on the ecology, natural history, management, and conservation biology of amphibians and reptiles. The focus stresses importance of natural history to conservation efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscript topics considered include natural history (behavior, parasitology, physiology), ecology, sampling design and techniques, field studies, inventories, long-term monitoring, and management case studies. Manuscripts with strong applied conservation objectives or implications that employ genetic techniques as tools will be considered. Contact Section Editor if unsure of suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity, equity, and inclusion commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal welcomes and encourages submissions by all authors regardless of ethnicity, gender identity/expression, national origin, or other characteristics and acknowledges implicit biases in peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journal commits to increase diversity on governing and editorial boards, disseminate educational information to editors and reviewers about peer-review biases and ways to reduce them, and strive for more equitable peer-review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author Submission Form required
rubrics_metrics.description: Each manuscript submitted must be accompanied by an Author Submission Form (PDF available on journal website).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide the Author Submission Form will result in the manuscript being returned without review. The corresponding author must also address items in the Statement of Authorship in the submission email or cover letter, and may provide suggested reviewers there.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript submission method and file type
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts must be submitted electronically as Microsoft Word (MSWord) documents to the appropriate Section Editor(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section Editors' contact emails are provided. Low-resolution figures/images should be embedded in the MS Word manuscript; high-resolution images will be required upon acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymization / blinded review
rubrics_metrics.description: Section Editors will remove as much identifying information as possible and send manuscripts to peer reviewers without identifying information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifying information includes author names/affiliations/biographies/acknowledgments and metadata in files. Authors may submit a redacted version (without identifying info) along with a complete version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of contributions / manuscript categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted categories: (1) Research Articles (includes techniques papers); (2) Forums (invited: critical reviews, rebuttals); (3) Invited Papers; (4) HerpSpectives; (5) Point-Counterpoint; (6) Classics in Herpetology; (7) Monographs (not accepted at this time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forums are invited and should state why review is needed; Reviews duplicating previous work or adding little will be rejected. HerpSpectives should be balanced and avoid tirades or one-sided arguments; Point-Counterpoint must be professional and non-confrontational.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript length limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit manuscripts to 30 pages of text (Times New Roman 12 pt., double spaced, 1-inch margins).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Literature Cited, Tables, Figures, author biosketches, and Appendices are excluded from this limit. Long tables that run onto a second formatted page will be presented in an appendix. Appendices exceeding five pages presented as a separate Supplemental Information PDF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsuitable topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts not accepted: short notes describing unique/rare observations (e.g., Natural History Notes), book reviews, species descriptions, checklists, species accounts, county records, manuscripts focused on systematics/phylogeny, and ecological modeling papers unless study includes extensive new field sampling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors whose topics are borderline should contact Section Editors for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Authorship / originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must attest manuscripts are original and no portion has been published elsewhere; corresponding author must affirm work is not under consideration elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theses and dissertations do not normally constitute prior publication. Corresponding author must assure every listed author contributed significantly (significant contribution implies active participation in at least three of: conceptual, data collection, analyses, writing manuscript, editing manuscript). Submission implies consent to open-access distribution of published paper, including photographs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer suggestions and exclusion requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may submit names of one or more potential peer reviewers or request to avoid specific parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection of peer reviewers remains at sole discretion of editors; requests to avoid specific reviewers will be considered but not guaranteed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance / peer-review decision criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptance contingent upon at least two favorable recommendations from anonymous peer reviewers and concurrence of the Associate and Section Editors assigned to the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reviews are mixed, Associate Editor may send manuscript to a third peer reviewer or review it themselves. Final acceptance rests with the Section Editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer reviewer forms / confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers will be asked to complete a Confidentiality Form upon accepting to review; comments submitted on the Peer Review Form in PDF format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To save the PDF forms, reviewers/editors must have Adobe Reader (Version 8 or later). Associate Editor will check Author Submission Form for inconsistencies upon receipt of reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision timeline policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Revisions received after six months will be treated as new submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponding author may request an extension from the appropriate Section Editor if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Galley proofs response time
rubrics_metrics.description: Galley proofs will be provided to corresponding author prior to publication; authors must respond within 48 h with any corrections required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authors do not respond within 48 h, the manuscript may be withheld until the next issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance rate (informational)
rubrics_metrics.description: In recent years, the acceptance rate for manuscripts submitted to Herpetological Conservation and Biology was 50%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is provided as contextual information, not as an evaluative rubric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and active-voice requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts must be written in English, clear, concise, and written primarily in the active voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given (active: 'We set traps at random locations...' vs passive: 'Traps were set at random locations...'). Authors who fail to use an active voice will be required to rewrite entire sections, even if detected at final copy edit stage, causing delays. Non-native English authors are strongly encouraged to have manuscripts proofed by an English-speaking colleague. A second abstract in another language may be included at authors' discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spelling, abbreviations, acronyms, and number conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use United States spelling. Common Latin abbreviations (et al., i.e., e.g.) should not be italicized; other Latin terms (in vitro, ad libitum, in situ, op. cit., sensu stricto) are italicized. Acronyms should be defined on first use. Do not start sentences with abbreviations; spell out numbers one through nine in running text and use numerals for 10 onward. When numbers are followed by units of measurement, use numerals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 1,968 ha; 0.3 kg; 3.7 m; 11 km; 5-y period. Sentences beginning with a number should have the number spelled out. Use SI units and present temperature in Celsius (25° C). Geographic coordinates may be Latitude/Longitude or UTM with zone. Note that abbreviations of scientific names retain italics (e.g., Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis (Bd)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended style manuals
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard reference for English stylistic and grammatical conventions is the Chicago Manual of Style; authors may also consult Scientific Style and Format: The CSE Manual for Authors, Editors, and Publishers (2014).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript general formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Whole manuscript must be double-spaced (includes tables, table and figure headings, and Literature Cited). Use Times New Roman 12 pt (including figures axis labels and tables). Text left justified; do not right-justify. All manuscript pages consecutively numbered at bottom center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective authors are encouraged to consult recently published HerpConBio articles for style. Manuscripts that do not closely follow these style guidelines and format will be returned without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short title requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a short title (maximum 60 characters including spaces) to be used as a running header.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title style and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Title should be brief yet informative, convey focus of investigation, and preferably include scientific name(s) of species studied. Scientific names should be in italics. The first letter of each word composing a specific common name should be capitalized (e.g., American Crocodile) but not when referring to the group (e.g., painted turtles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Titles should be centered, 16-point font, bolded, and in large and small capitals Times New Roman.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author listing format
rubrics_metrics.description: List author names followed by affiliations and indicate corresponding author by footnotes on separate lines, in italics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use abbreviations in street addresses, state/province and country, except 'USA'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An abstract is required for all manuscripts and should be a concise summary of objectives, results, and conclusions written in layman's terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract text should be bolded, begin with 'Abstract.—' in boldface italics, and should not exceed 250 words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key words formatting and content
rubrics_metrics.description: A maximum of eight key words reflecting main aspects of the investigation; should not include words already in the title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short phrases or names (e.g., 'Eastern Garter Snake') count as one key word. Key words should include common and scientific names and primary topics, listed in alphabetical order, plain font, separated by semicolons, forming a new paragraph immediately after the Abstract. Heading should be two words, in italics (not bolded), followed by a period and em dash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required manuscript section order and heading styles
rubrics_metrics.description: First page: Short Title, title, authors/affiliations, Abstract, Key Words. Subsequent pages: INTRODUCTION, MATERIALS AND METHODS, RESULTS, DISCUSSION, Acknowledgments, LITERATURE CITED, Tables, Figures, Appendices (as applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major section headings should be in small caps, boldface, and centered. The Short Title, Abstract, Key Words, and Acknowledgments should be lower case, italicized, and followed by a period and em dash. Acknowledgments should be indented by 0.33 cm. Section sub-headings should begin a new paragraph, boldface, italicized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduction should acquaint the reader with the present state of knowledge through judicious use of citations; not exhaustive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usually five citations are sufficient; authors should state significance (how manuscript addresses a void) and end with clear statement of specific objectives or hypotheses tested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials and Methods detail and sensitive locality handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide sufficient level of detail to ensure future repeating of the study; descriptions of study sites belong in this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precise locality data (lat/long) for Special Concern/Threatened/Endangered species should not be included in the manuscript; deposit such data at an established museum or secure institution referenced in the text. Dates format as '29 March 2006'. Time unit abbreviations y, mo, d, h, min, s. Use 24-hour time with no colons (e.g., 0956). Indicate methods used to evaluate assumptions of all statistical tests and whether assumptions were met. Lengthy methods can be provided as an appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results content and statistical reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Results section should include neither raw data nor interpretations or conclusions; summarize data using statistics, tables, and/or figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statistical results format examples: (Z = 1.395, df = 3, P = 0.040). Capitalize and italicize statistical test statistics except those requiring lower-case and use subscript where appropriate (e.g., t = 2.453, df = 4.5, P = 0.031 or r = 0.13, t = 3.142, P < 0.001). Do not capitalize or italicize degrees of freedom. Report mean ± SE or SD and range as: mean SVL = 14.3 ± (SE) 1.6 mm (range, 12.2–16.5 mm) with sample sizes presented as n = 25. Separate number ranges with an en dash and ensure consistent significant figures. Use 'SE' and 'SD' without periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables and figures numbering and captions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Arabic numerals to number each table and figure sequentially. Self-explanatory captions must accompany each table and figure and be capable of standing alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table captions placed at top of tables; figure captions placed below figures. Include species common and scientific names and study location in captions if appropriate. No need to list them sequentially on a separate page preceding the figures. Footnotes allowed sparingly for tables only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure formatting, size, and legibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Times Roman font for all lettering; axes must be black. Figures containing histograms, pie charts, line graphs, etc. must have legible text when reduced to journal width.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single column figures ~80 mm (3.18 in) wide; double column not to exceed 165 mm (6.5 in). Authors should check figure clarity at journal size in Word by changing width to recommended size before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure file formats, resolution, and photographic manipulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs may be in color or black and white. Figures should be low-resolution (not to exceed 2 MB) .png, .tif, or .jpg files embedded within the manuscript submitted for consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple graphs/photographs combined as one image should be formatted by authors and labeled A, B, C... in captions. High-resolution images will be required by Section Editor upon acceptance. Any electronic manipulations/enhancements to original digital photographs must be disclosed in the figure title. Photographer credit must be provided (e.g., 'Photographed by John L. Behler').

rubrics_metrics.name: Maps requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Maps are figures and must include a legend, scale bar, and cardinal direction indicator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maps should include data source information in the caption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table creation and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must create tables using the Tables function in MS Word (or similar).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Times New Roman font size 12 for tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendices and long tables policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Long tables that run onto a second formatted page should be presented in an appendix. Appendices exceeding five pages will be presented as a separate Supplemental Information PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appendices are less than one page, author biographies should follow them; if appendices are more than one page, bios should precede the appendices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental Information policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental Information may include additional material useful to the reader but not necessary to understand the paper; this material will not be reviewed or edited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At Section Editor and Copy Editor discretion, supplemental info may be placed at end of article and not paginated or linked as a separate PDF. Translations of the manuscript may be supplied by authors as supplemental information with a qualifying statement: 'This translation is provided by the authors and is based on the final accepted English version of the paper. The journal did not edit the translation.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Author photographs and biosketch requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon acceptance, authors should provide a photograph of each author (.png or .jpg) and a brief biography (max 180 words).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If more than three authors, limit biosketches to 90 words or fewer. For manuscripts with many authors, group photos or featuring only prominent authors is allowed. Include photographer name as described for figure credits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photo gallery submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of accepted manuscripts are encouraged to submit up to 20 high-quality digital images for the online photo gallery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Image files must be of highest resolution possible. Inclusion is at the discretion of the Photo Gallery Section Editor. Copyright retained by photographer. Photo gallery URL provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature Cited strict formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should strictly adhere to the citation formats presented; failure demonstrates lack of attention to detail and may increase scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No empty lines between references. First line left justified with hanging indent 0.33 cm for subsequent lines. Only one space between citation elements; no spaces between author initials. The order is alphabetical then chronological. For same first author: single author, two authors, three or more authors. Order multi-authored papers alphabetically. If >10 authors, list first 10 then et al. Use en dashes without adjacent spaces to separate numerals. Capitalize specific common names in citations. Books/theses may include country of publication (spell out country names except USA and UK).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited and sparing citation types
rubrics_metrics.description: Conference abstracts and submitted (not yet accepted) manuscripts should not be cited in Literature Cited. Personal communications and unpublished/non peer-reviewed reports should be cited sparingly in running text rather than included in Literature Cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should not cite their own unpublished reports in Literature Cited; they should summarize such information or place it in an appendix or submit it as a manuscript to the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Website citation rules and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Websites should be cited sparingly in running text using a provided format and ensure hyperlinks work prior to submittal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a website is cited more than once, abbreviate subsequent citations (op. cit.). Exceptions: IUCN and R statistical package citations should be included in Literature Cited. For these web sites, do not list an accessed date; treat similarly to online journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Object Identifier (DOI) policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Herpetological Conservation and Biology does not subscribe to, participate in, or issue DOI numbers for manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons: cost to issue DOIs, CrossRef/for-profit publisher infrastructure and limited benefit to readers given paywalls, and desire to remain truly open-access without fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove bibliographic software formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors using bibliographic software (EndNote, Zotero, Mendeley, Sente, etc.) should remove all bibliographic formatting from the manuscript prior to submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors and reviewers cannot edit or make comments in Literature Cited when program codes are present. Failure to remove this formatting will result in manuscripts being returned without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical notation conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalization and italicization rules for statistical test statistics and presentation of P values and degrees of freedom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (Z = 1.395, df = 3, P = 0.040). Use subscript where appropriate (e.g., t = 2.453, df = 4.5). Do not capitalize or italicize degrees of freedom. Use exact P-values where appropriate and consistent formatting for test statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbered list formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbered lists should be formatted with: (1) more than two items long; (2) semi-colons between items; and (3) parentheses on both sides of the numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence spacing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should verify that there are exactly two spaces between all sentences in the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are no sentences in the Literature Cited; therefore, nothing should be separated by two spaces in this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure caption content expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Captions should be self-explanatory and capable of standing alone without accompanying text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include species common and scientific names and location of study in captions, if appropriate. Place table captions at top and figure captions below figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: All copyrights remain with the first author of a published manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission implies consent to open-access distribution by the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission acknowledgement timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Section Editors should acknowledge receipt of a manuscript within 7 days of submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If corresponding author does not receive a timely response, contact the Editor-in-Chief to confirm receipt.
